options.why: Used the female formula constant of $5.5$ instead of $6.8$.
Omitted the metabolism term $7.5H$ from the numerator.

questions.question_text: Ben ($70\text{ kg}$ male) and Lucy ($70\text{ kg}$ female) both consume $4$ standard drinks over $3\text{ hours}$. Which statement correctly compares their estimated BAC values?

options.text: Lucy has a higher BAC than Ben because the female formula uses a smaller denominator constant ($5.5$) reflecting lower average body water.
Ben has a higher BAC than Lucy because the male formula uses a larger denominator constant ($6.8$).
options.why: Confused the effect of the denominator; a larger denominator produces a smaller BAC.

options.text: Ben and Lucy have the exact same BAC because they have the same mass and consumed the same drinks.
options.why: Ignored the sex-specific formula constants representing average body water differences.

options.text: Lucy has a higher BAC because her body metabolises alcohol at $5.5\text{ g/h}$ instead of $7.5\text{ g/h}$.
options.why: Confused the body mass factor $5.5$ with the hourly metabolic rate $7.5$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \dfrac{10(4) - 7.5(3)}{6.8(70)} = \dfrac{17.5}{476} \approx 0.037$
$\text{BAC}_{\text{female}} = \dfrac{10(4) - 7.5(3)}{5.5(70)} = \dfrac{17.5}{385} \approx 0.045$
Lucy has the higher estimated BAC.
